evals.prompt: the pricing page at https://app.northwind-metrics.io/plans is all client-side React, curl just gives me an empty <div id=root>. I have a browserless instance configured via env vars. Pull the rendered HTML, wait for .plan-card to appear, and save it to /tmp/plans.html, then tell me the three plan prices.
evals.expected_output: Agent POSTs to the /content endpoint with waitForSelector, saves the HTML, runs the empty-body and Chrome error-page check, then reports the prices from the real page.
expectations: The instance URL and token are read from BROWSERLESS_URL and BROWSERLESS_TOKEN and never appear as literal values in a command
The /content endpoint (or /scrape with selectors) is called with the target URL via POST with a JSON body and token as query parameter
The request body sets waitForSelector for .plan-card
The output is written to /tmp/plans.html and its size or markup is checked for an empty body or Chrome error page before use
No local Chrome or Puppeteer install is attempted

evals.prompt: My CI runner is an alpine container with no Chrome. I need a full-page PNG screenshot of https://staging.acme-shop.dev/checkout saved to artifacts/checkout.png and an A4 PDF of the same page saved to artifacts/checkout.pdf. The remote headless chrome token is in the environment.
evals.expected_output: Agent calls /screenshot with fullPage and /pdf with format A4 using curl -sf, writes both files to the named paths, and confirms their types with file.
expectations: A preflight check or explicit statement verifies BROWSERLESS_URL and BROWSERLESS_TOKEN are set, and the values are not hardcoded
The /screenshot endpoint is called with options fullPage true and type png
The /pdf endpoint is called with format A4 and printBackground
Outputs are written to artifacts/checkout.png and artifacts/checkout.pdf, and curl uses -f so HTTP errors are not saved as artifacts
The file types are confirmed (for example with the file command) before reporting success

evals.prompt: Use browserless to unblock https://news.ycombinator.com past any bot wall and give me the rendered HTML. Our instance is the self-hosted open-source image.
evals.expected_output: Agent probes /unblock, sees 404 on the self-hosted instance, does not retry or vary the path, reports that it is cloud-only, and falls back to /content with stealth while verifying the result.
expectations: The agent probes the /unblock endpoint and checks the HTTP status code before relying on it
On a 404 the agent does not retry or try path variants, and tells the user /unblock is cloud-only and unavailable on this instance
Any fallback to /content uses stealth launch and blockAds, and is not presented as an /unblock result
The fallback HTML is checked for a Chrome error page, empty body, or bot-wall text before being summarized
Credentials are read from environment variables and never appear literally
